back: Home trade: buying and selling within one country. Foreign trade: exchange of goods and services between countries.
Concentrating resources on the goods a country produces most efficiently and trading for the rest.
Exports: goods/services sold to other countries (money in). Imports: goods/services bought from other countries (money out).

front: Give four differences between home and foreign trade.
back: Currency exchange; distance and transport; customs laws and documents; language and culture; greater risk.

front: Give four advantages of international trade.
back: Access to goods not produced at home; lower prices; more choice; larger markets and economies of scale; foreign currency; competition; technology.

front: Give four disadvantages of international trade and specialisation.
back: Dependence on a few exports; dependence on imported essentials; closure of local firms; exchange rate risk; harm to infant industries.

front: Is spending by foreign tourists in Zimbabwe an export or an import?
back: An (invisible) export of services: money flows into Zimbabwe.

front: Why is a landlocked country at a disadvantage in foreign trade?
back: Goods must travel through other countries to reach ports, adding transport costs and delays.
